Probioticsfor plants: Helpful bacteria promote growth, less fertilizer on crops

This endophyte-plant relationship is partly a matter of speed in adaptation. "Plants have a limited ability to genetically adapt to rapid environmental changes (heat, drought, toxins, or limited nutrients) and so they may use microbes that do have this capacity to rapidly evolve due to their vastly shorter life cycles," she explained. "By having the right microbes for the conditions, the plants are healthier. That is how it is similar to humans taking probiotics to improve their health."
I know of organic farmers that have used bio-active teas for a good while now. It would be super cool to see this catch on at a business level!

This is an interesting approach to increasing crop production without having to add even more fertilizers to the mix. Although I have to ask, what are the impacts on local bacterial populations? Is there a possibility of causing invasive species to flourish by using pre-packaged "microbe seeders" in fields?
Local bacterial populations plummet on farms due to modern farming practices. It's a known problem that's only recently been getting some attention. So I imagine this would help more than hurt.
